Worried your favourite Youtuber will be banned and all of their content removed forever? Me too.

This guide is for any debian-based Linux. Mint or Ubuntu will do fine. Extremely basic Linux terminal skills are required.

At the terminal, type:

sudo apt install youtube-dl

Once it's done installing, create the following text file in your favourite editor, like nano. Call it something like 'download'.

#!/bin/bash
youtube-dl -o '%(uploader)s/%(uploader)s - %(title)s.%(ext)s' \
-f "best[height=720]/best" \
--write-description --write-info-json --write-annotations -w --write-thumbnail \
--min-sleep-interval 2 --max-sleep-interval 360 $1

Make your script executable

chmod a+x download

Invoke the script like so:

./download https://www.youtube.com/user/PewDiePie/videos

The URL should be the videos section of a channel or a playlist.

By default, youtube-dl will attempt to resume aborted downloads and will not overwrite existing files, so you can ctrl-c to kill it and then run it again to resume later. You can also use the ctrl-z trick to suspend, then issue a single % to resume. This is quicker but state does not persist through restart.

This part of the script controls where the files are saved to:

'%(uploader)s/%(uploader)s - %(title)s.%(ext)s'

This is a relative path, so it stores stuff wherever you run the script from as I'm sure you've seen.

You can just put the script on your spinning HDD, or you can change the path to an absolute one that references another drive. On my system it would look like this:

'/media/curious/fatty_4tb/%(uploader)s/%(uploader)s - %(title)s.%(ext)s'

To put specific youtubers in specific locations will require a bit more scripting magic.
